facts.text: The brown quail is also known as the swamp quail, silver quail and Tasmanian quail.
facts.quote: The brown quail (Synoicus ypsilophorus), also known as the swamp quail, silver quail and Tasmanian quail, is an Australasian true quail of the family Phasianidae.

facts.text: This plump, stocky bird grows up to 17 to 22 centimetres long and weighs 75 to 140 grams.
facts.quote: The brown quail is a plump, stocky bird which can grow up to a length of 17 to 22 centimetres (6+1⁄2 to 8+1⁄2 in) and weight of 75 to 140 grams (2+3⁄4 to 5 oz).

facts.text: The male is reddish-brown speckled with black on the head and upper neck, with black chevron-shaped barring on its underparts.
facts.quote: The male is reddish-brown speckled with black on the head and upper neck and mainly reddish-brown on back and wings. The underparts range from buff or rufous to brown, but always with fine black chevron-shaped barring.

facts.text: The female is paler than the male, with small black spots on her shoulder and dark chevron-shaped markings on her upperparts.
facts.quote: The female is similar but rather paler. There are small black spots on the shoulder of the female and the upperparts are barred with dark chevron-shaped markings.

facts.text: Brown quails communicate with shrill calls as they move through dense vegetation, including a double whistle whose second note ascends.
facts.quote: The voice consists of a variety of shrill calls with which the birds communicate as they move through dense vegetation.  One call is a double whistle, the latter note ascending.

facts.text: When a group of brown quails is startled into the air, they scatter in different directions and regroup once the danger has passed.
facts.quote: If the group is startled and take to the air, the birds scatter by flying in different directions, regrouping when the danger has passed.

facts.text: Brown quail are ground-dwellers that would rather hide or run than fly, and feed on grasses, seeds, shoots and small invertebrates.
facts.quote: The brown quail is a ground-dwelling bird that prefers to hide or run rather than fly. It is found in small groups and feeds on grasses, seeds, shoots and small invertebrates.

facts.text: Brown quails nest on the ground in a shallow scrape lined with grasses, often hidden in a grass tussock or shrubby bush.
facts.quote: clutches of half a dozen or more eggs being laid in a shallow scraped nest lined with grasses on the ground, often concealed in a grass tussock or shrubby bush

facts.text: The female incubates the eggs for three weeks, and after two weeks the male takes over chick care so she can start the next clutch.
facts.quote: These are incubated by the female for the three-week incubation period. The newly hatched chicks are precocial and are cared for by both parents for a while, with the male taking on the caring role after two weeks to allow the female to start on the next clutch of eggs.

facts.text: The Kunwinjku people of western Arnhem Land call this bird djirndih, djiribbidj or merhmerh.
facts.quote: The Kunwinjku people of western Arnhem Land call this bird djirndih, djiribbidj or merhmerh (all quails).
